researchQuestion: Does directed access to Human Standards through MCP change the quality of an AI-built clinic appointment interface?

conditions.C: Frozen Human Standards context packet without MCP

protocolDeviation.planned: Two independent reviewers would each score all nine opaque artifacts before the condition mapping was revealed.
protocolDeviation.completed: The project coordinator conducted an initially condition-blind qualitative walkthrough. No independent reviewer completed the frozen rubric and no P3 human-centred quality score was calculated.
protocolDeviation.decision: The pilot was concluded before external review because it already exposed material cross-condition failures and no consistently superior experience. The nine outputs are now treated as a development set, not confirmatory evidence.

coordinatorObservations: The flow starts directly on booking rather than a separate landing page; this is not inherently a defect.
Appointment radio cards did not expose a usable keyboard focus experience during the walkthrough.
The first date and Email contact method were preselected.
A missing-name validation message appeared at the bottom of the form without marking or placing the message beside the field.
The stepper was clear and well spaced.
The confirmation copy claimed an email would be sent even though the fictional service sends no message.
The landing page and four-step vertical flow were visually distinctive and easy to orient within.
Selecting an appointment type advanced immediately, which is efficient but consequential.
Arrow-key navigation was not available between time choices presented as a related selection set.
Home-page buttons had no visible hover treatment, pointer affordance or reliable keyboard focus indicator.
Appointment cards lacked visible radio affordance, hover treatment and a usable keyboard focus experience.
Form labels and entered values used similar heavy emphasis, weakening hierarchy.
The rescheduling path did not provide a clear post-commit success screen.
The stepper was well aligned and spaced.
The landing page was polished, although its hero buttons and lower cards repeated the same two actions.
Appointment-type radio cards did not expose a usable keyboard focus experience during the walkthrough.
The existing-booking action was unusually prominent and easy to discover.
Entered data was retained when moving backwards and forwards.
The confirmation details were well organised.
The progress steps were visually cramped.
The current-step treatment had weak separation from the page background and the progress labels were not evenly aligned.

During the walkthrough, Physiotherapy times displayed a non-injected loading failure and Retry did not recover. A later fresh launch did not reproduce the same state, so this is reported as an observed reliability warning rather than a deterministic defect.
The interface correctly refused to continue without an available date and time.
The confirmation layout was streamlined.
Appointment and time selection controls did not expose a usable keyboard focus experience.
A date dropdown added interaction cost for only two available dates.
Email was preselected.
The two home-page cards had uneven dimensions and the urgent-care icon was visually compressed.
The main call to action had no visible hover treatment.
Selected appointment states shifted neighbouring content.
The review transition did not return focus or scroll position to the top.
Review and confirmation details used tight spacing and centre alignment that reduced scanability.
The simple home page stood out positively and the review screen spacing was effective.
Appointment radio cards did not expose a usable keyboard focus experience.
Available-time headings and controls were tightly spaced.
Confirmation details were unnecessarily centre aligned.
Exit to home and Return to home repeated the same action.

crossArtifactFindings: Keyboard and focus behaviour remained a recurring weakness in every condition.
Run-to-run variation was large enough to complicate any simple treatment story.
Polished visual hierarchy did not guarantee complete booking-management behaviour.
All nine runs failed the non-critical refresh-safety scenario F12.
The directed MCP condition was directionally strongest on automated outcomes, but did not produce a uniformly strong human experience.

humanOutcome.reason: No independent rubric reviews were completed. Coordinator observations are qualitative and must not be substituted for the preregistered blinded human-centred quality score.
